---
title: "cppFUN() and its derivative directions"
---

`cppFUN()` compiles a system of algebraic expressions
[]{#eq-funcpp}
$$
  y_i = g_i(x_1, \dots, x_{n_x}, p_1, \dots, p_{n_p}),
  \qquad i = 1, \dots, n_y, \tag{52}
$$
with its first and second derivatives and no time integration. The
variables $x$ are the rows of an $n_{\mathrm{obs}} \times n_x$ matrix,
one per observation; the parameters $p$ are shared by all rows. Typical
uses are observation maps, which connect integrator output to data and
whose derivatives enter the gradient of a likelihood, and
reparametrisations $p = \Phi(\theta)$, whose Jacobian is the tangent of
[(13)](methods-forward.html#eq-sensitivity-theta).

The expressions are parsed into the [expression graph](methods-codegen.html#codegen), from which the generator emits one function template
over the scalar type that evaluates $g$ for one observation, instantiated
on `double`, on `cppde::dual<double, 0>` and on the nested
dual `cppde::dual2nd<double, 0>`. The vector-Jacobian product is
a reverse sweep on the same graph, emitted as a second template and
instantiated on `double` and on the dual.

Every entry runs compiled code. With the default `compile = FALSE`
the constructor only writes the source; the object must be passed to
`compile()` before use, and its functions stop with an error
until then.

## Entry points and derivative directions

`derivMode` names the derivative products built, any of
`"forward"`, the default, `"reverse"` and
`"forward-reverse"`, which implies `"reverse"`. A product left
out costs no entries and no compile time. `deriv`
and `deriv2` switch the first- and second-order entries;
`deriv2 = TRUE` requires `"forward"`. The R functions of the returned
object and the compiled entries they call are

| R function | direction | compiled entry |
|:-------------------------|:--------|:------------|
| `func(x, p)` | any | `_eval_c` |
| `jac(x, p[, tangentX, tangentP])` | forward | `_eval_ad_c` |
| `hess(x, p[, tangentX, tangentP, hessianX, hessianP])` | forward | `_eval_ad2_c` |
| `evaluate(..., deriv2)` | forward | `_eval_ad_c` or `_eval_ad2_c` |
| `evaluateBatch(sets, cores, deriv2)` | forward | `_eval_ad_batch` or `_eval_ad2_batch` |
| `vjp(x, p, cotangent)` | reverse | `_vjp_c` |
| `vjp(x, p, cotangent, tangentX, tangentP, curvature)` | forward-reverse | `_vjp_ad_c` |

Table: R functions of a `cppFUN()` object and the compiled entries they
call, each prefixed by the model name; `x` and `p` stand for the
arguments `vars` and `params`. The `_c` entries are `.Call` interfaces
that take their arguments by reference; `_eval`, `_eval_ad`, `_eval_ad2`
and `_vjp` also exist as `.C` interfaces, used only for a shared object
without the `.Call` symbol. Under `"forward-reverse"`, `_vjp_ad` is also
a plain C entry that native code can call from its own threads.

**Forward direction.** `jac` evaluates $g$ on duals and
returns $\partial y/\partial\theta$ as an array
$[n_{\mathrm{obs}}, n_y, n_\theta]$; `hess` evaluates it on
nested duals and returns $\partial^2 y/\partial\theta^2$ as
$[n_{\mathrm{obs}}, n_y, n_\theta, n_\theta]$. The directions $\theta$
are set by the tangents of the next section. Without them the identity
over the variables and the differentiated parameters is used, which
gives the Jacobian or Hessian with respect to $(x, p)$.
`evaluate` returns value and derivatives from one pass as
`y`, `tangent` and, with `deriv2 = TRUE`,
`hessian`; separate calls of `func`, `jac` and
`hess` would evaluate $g$ up to three times.
`evaluateBatch` runs `evaluate` over a list of argument
sets in one call, distributed over OpenMP threads with dynamic
scheduling, and falls back to a loop for fewer than two sets.
`evaluateMany()` does the same for argument sets each with its own
`cppFUN()` object, in one parallel region.

**Reverse direction.** For a cotangent $w$ of the outputs,
$[n_{\mathrm{obs}}, n_y]$ or $[n_{\mathrm{obs}}, n_y, n_{\mathrm{seed}}]$,
`vjp` returns
[]{#eq-funcpp-vjp}
$$
  (w_x)_{o j s} = \sum_{i} w_{o i s}\,
      \frac{\partial g_i}{\partial x_j}(x_o, p),
  \qquad
  (w_p)_{k s} = \sum_{o} \sum_{i} w_{o i s}\,
      \frac{\partial g_i}{\partial p_k}(x_o, p), \tag{53}
$$
as `cotangentX` and `cotangentP`, together with the value
$y$; the parameter part sums over the observations, which share $p$.
The contraction is one reverse sweep per observation and cotangent
column, at a cost independent of the number of upstream parameters, and
forms neither the Jacobian nor the Hessian. Statements of the sweep
that do not depend on the cotangent are evaluated once per observation,
outside the loop over cotangent columns.

Given the tangents $v_x$ and $v_p$ of the inputs in $n_{\mathrm{dir}}$
directions as `tangentX` and `tangentP`, or the
derivative $\dot w$ of the cotangent along them as `curvature`,
`vjp` runs the same template on duals and additionally returns
[]{#eq-funcpp-vjp-curvature}
$$
  \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}v}\bigl(w^{\mathsf T} J\bigr)
    = w^{\mathsf T}\,\frac{\partial J}{\partial (x, p)}\,v
      + \dot w^{\mathsf T} J,
  \qquad J = \frac{\partial g}{\partial (x, p)}, \tag{54}
$$
as `curvatureX` and `curvatureP`. This is forward over
reverse (see [second derivatives](methods-forward-reverse.html)): an observation map contributes its
curvature to a backward chain without forming a Hessian.

## Tangent, hessian, cotangent and curvature

A map has a tangent and a Hessian, a functional a cotangent and a
curvature. For the upstream map $\Phi: \theta \mapsto (x, p)$ these are
the `tangent` $\partial\Phi(\theta)$ and the `hessian`
$\partial^2\Phi(\theta)$; for a scalar functional $L$ of the outputs
$y$, the `cotangent` $\partial L(y)$ and the `curvature`
$\partial^2 L(y)\,\partial y$, the derivative of the cotangent along the
tangent. An argument and its result share a name (table below): a forward argument lives on the inputs and
its result on the outputs, a reverse argument on the outputs and its
result on the inputs.

| `solveODE()` | `cppFUN()` argument | `cppFUN()` result |
|:-------------|:--------------------|:------------------|
| `tangent`   | `tangentX`, `tangentP` | `tangent` |
| `hessian`   | `hessianX`, `hessianP` | `hessian` |
| `cotangent` | `cotangent`            | `cotangentX`, `cotangentP` |
| `curvature` | `curvature`            | `curvatureX`, `curvatureP` |

Table: Names of the four derivative objects in R. `solveODE()` uses one
name for the argument and the element of its result; the `cppFUN()`
results are elements of the lists that `evaluate` and `vjp` return.

Forward over forward takes the `hessian` of the inputs and
returns that of the outputs, the second derivatives of every output in
every pair of tangent directions. Forward over reverse takes the
`curvature` of the outputs and returns that of the inputs, the
Hessian of the seeded functional applied to the tangent, or, with the
identity tangent, the columns of that Hessian.

**Chain rule.** `cppFUN()` takes the tangent and the hessian
of its inputs in two blocks each:

- `tangentX[obs, name, theta]`: $\partial x_i/\partial\theta_a$,
  per observation row, variable and direction $\theta_a$;
- `tangentP[name, theta]`: $\partial p_j/\partial\theta_a$, the
  same for all observations;
- `hessianX[obs, name, theta1, theta2]`:
  $\partial^2 x_i/\partial\theta_a\partial\theta_b$, optional, zero by
  default;
- `hessianP[name, theta1, theta2]`:
  $\partial^2 p_j/\partial\theta_a\partial\theta_b$, optional, zero by
  default.

They may also be supplied as the attributes `deriv` and
`deriv2` of the variables and parameters. Tangent rows of
parameters in `fixed` are zero, and symbols absent from the
tangent contribute zero.

With the tangent $\partial\Phi \in \mathbb{R}^{n_{\mathrm{obs}} \times
n_{\mathrm{diff}} \times n_\theta}$ over the
$n_{\mathrm{diff}} = n_x + n_p$ inputs and the hessian $\partial^2\Phi$,
the chain rule gives the Jacobian
$$
  \frac{\partial y}{\partial\theta}\bigg|_{\mathrm{obs}}
    = J\bigl(x_{\mathrm{obs}}, p\bigr) \cdot \partial\Phi_{\mathrm{obs}}, \tag{55}
$$
and the Hessian of output $i$
$$
  \frac{\partial^2 y_i}{\partial\theta\,\partial\theta^{\mathsf T}}\bigg|_{\mathrm{obs}}
    = \partial\Phi_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\mathsf T} \, H_i\bigl(x_{\mathrm{obs}}, p\bigr) \,
      \partial\Phi_{\mathrm{obs}}
    + \sum_{j} J_{i, j}\bigl(x_{\mathrm{obs}}, p\bigr) \,
        \partial^2\Phi_{\mathrm{obs}, j, \cdot, \cdot}, \tag{56}
$$
whose second term vanishes when $\Phi$ is affine.

Neither $J$ nor $H$ is formed: both contractions follow from seeding
the tangent slots of the duals. Each input scalar $x_i$ becomes
$$
  \tilde x_i = (x_i + \partial\Phi_{i,\cdot}\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{in}})
             + \bigl(\partial\Phi_{i,\cdot}
                     + \partial^2\Phi_{i,\cdot,\cdot}\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{in}}\bigr)\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out}},
$$
a nested dual whose inner tangent slots hold $\partial x_i/\partial\theta$
and whose outer tangent slot $k$ is an inner dual with value
$\partial x_i/\partial\theta_k$ and inner tangents
$\partial^2 x_i/\partial\theta_k\partial\theta$. The multiplication rule
then propagates the $\partial\Phi^{\mathsf T} H\, \partial\Phi$ and
$J \cdot \partial^2\Phi$ terms in one evaluation; the inner tangents of
$\tilde y$ are $\partial y/\partial\theta$, and the cross slots
$\tilde y[k][m]$ are $\partial^2 y/\partial\theta_k\partial\theta_m$.

## Pass-through of unmodelled inputs

With `attach.input = TRUE`, inputs that do not appear among the
variables and parameters of [(52)](#eq-funcpp) are appended to the output
unchanged: their values are copied, their Jacobian rows are zero for a
variable and the identity for a parameter, and their Hessian rows are
zero. An observation map then need not repeat every column of the
integrator output as an identity, as with the partial-shape
`tangent` of `solveODE()`.
